title: Zero Third-Party Dependencies Constraint in release.py and deploy.py
answers: Can I add external libraries (e.g. requests, httpx) to release.py or deploy.py?
Why does release.py use http.client instead of requests?
What dependencies are allowed in release automation scripts?
body:
Both `release/release.py` and `release/deploy.py` enforce a strict policy: `# Security: No third-party dependencies here!`.
All network calls in `release.py` use standard library `http.client` (e.g. `release/release.py:get`) or `urllib.request` rather than external dependencies like `requests` or `httpx` to minimize supply-chain exposure during credentialed release workflows.
Only Python standard library modules (`os`, `sys`, `json`, `re`, `subprocess`, `time`, `pathlib`) are permitted in these two scripts.
In contrast, `release/build.py` runs in build environments and permits build helpers like `click` and `cryptography.fernet`.
applies: Applies strictly to `release/release.py` and `release/deploy.py`; does not apply to `release/build.py`.
says: Release and deployment automation scripts should not depend on external third party packages.
Eliminate external package dependencies from release scripts to prevent supply chain security risks.
The package publishing workflow failed because an unauthorized external library was introduced.
Ensure the release pipeline relies strictly on built in tools for uploading distribution assets.
